advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'malformed applies_to ignored, never raised' claim with effective_routing's hard validation of applies_to (which runs on the same overlay during the review), or scope the claim to trigger_tokens only.
evidence: registry.py:262-264 docstring: 'Malformed values (non-list tokens, non-string elements, entries under an id not in OVERLAY_IDS) are ignored, never raised.'
overlay.py:206-210 _validate_applies_to raises CriteriaError when applies_to is not a list of non-empty glob strings

workflow_ops.py:418: `routing = registry.effective_routing(ctx.repo_root)` runs during the same code review, loading+validating the same overlay via _validate_routing_entry -> _validate_applies_to (overlay.py:272)
advisory.finding: The docstring/design promise that a malformed `applies_to` under a built-in overlay id is 'ignored, never raised' holds only for project_trigger_extensions in isolation; in the real review the same overlay is loaded via registry.effective_routing (workflow_ops.py:418), whose _validate_applies_to raises CriteriaError on a non-string/empty glob, so a malformed applies_to still aborts the review loudly.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether project trigger extensions should be restricted to glob/content-triggerable overlays (excluding scope-intent), or document that scope-intent in content/glob_overlays is advisory-only and not honored in to_run.
evidence: registry.py:273: `if cid not in OVERLAY_IDS or not isinstance(entry, dict): continue` — admits every OVERLAY_IDS id including 'scope-intent'

workflow_ops.py:107-109: `selected.discard("scope-intent")` then re-added only from scope_context, but out['content_overlays']=content_set / out['glob_overlays']=glob_set are the raw returned lists (workflow_ops.py:119-120)
advisory.finding: project_trigger_extensions accepts every OVERLAY_IDS member, so a project trigger_tokens/applies_to entry keyed on `scope-intent` (or deletion-impact/surface-parity) will surface that id in content_triggered_overlays/glob_triggered_overlays and hence in out['content_overlays']/out['glob_overlays'], even though overlay_union force-discards scope-intent from the actual to_run set.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider caching _load_overlay / project_trigger_extensions (or computing the extension once in overlay_union and passing it into both trigger calls) to avoid re-reading the overlay JSON multiple times per review.
evidence: registry.py:265-267: `from rebar.llm.criteria.overlay import _load_overlay` then `overlay = _load_overlay(repo_root)` — no memoization
overlay.py:167-187 _load_overlay reads+json.loads the file each call (no lru_cache)
registry.py:304 and registry.py:383 each independently call project_trigger_extensions(repo_root); workflow_ops.py:98-99 call both trigger functions per overlay_union
advisory.finding: _load_overlay is not cached, and it is now invoked once per trigger function; overlay_union calls both glob_triggered_overlays and content_triggered_overlays each of which calls project_trigger_extensions -> _load_overlay, so the overlay JSON is read+parsed twice per overlay_union invocation (and overlay_union runs twice per review), unlike effective_routing which is lru_cached.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where a project trigger_token matches only a `+++`/`---` header substring (e.g. token `b/x.py`) and assert the overlay does NOT fire.
evidence: Test tokens used: FROBNICATE(, HOTPATH(, OKTOKEN(, ZZZMARKER — none appears in a `+++ b/...`/`--- a/...` header line, so the header-skip branch is never asserted against.
ABSENCE: no test declares a trigger_token matching a substring of the diff's file-header path and asserts the overlay does NOT fire.
advisory.finding: No test verifies the stated header-exclusion contract: a project trigger_token that appears ONLY in a `+++`/`---` file-header line must NOT fire the overlay. The `_scan_project_tokens` loop and content_triggered_overlays docstring both explicitly promise the `+++`/`---` headers are excluded, but every test token is absent from the header lines, so a regression that let headers participate in matching would pass silently.
advisory.suggested_fix:
Add a test: root with {"performance": {"trigger_tokens": ["b/x.py"]}}, diff `--- a/x.py
+++ b/x.py
@@ ... @@
+    noop = 1
`, assert `"performance" not in reg.content_triggered_overlays(diff, root)`.
